review_comments.body:
The minutes check misses offset changes that are not on the hour. In `Pacific/Chatham` DST ends at 03:45 (+13:45 → +12:45), so a shift that crosses it still lands on minute 59, but in the previous local hour:

```js
// TZ=Pacific/Chatham
hourEnd(new Date("2026-04-04T13:18:13.123Z")) // input 03:03:13 +13:45
// this PR: 2026-04-04T14:14:59.999Z = 02:59:59.999 +12:45  (hour 2, input is hour 3)
// main:    2026-04-04T15:14:59.999Z = 03:59:59.999 +12:45
```

Checking the hour too fixes it and keeps the New York fix:

```ts
if (shifted.getMinutes() === 59 && shifted.getHours() === d.getHours()) return shifted
```

(same for `hourStart.ts`, with `=== 0`). I ran all 418 IANA zones, every transition 1990–2035, ±23 h around each: with this PR, `hourStart`/`hourEnd` return a different local hour than the input where main did not in Chatham, St_Johns, Goose_Bay, Moncton and Bishkek (~980 cases; e.g. Goose_Bay 1990-10-28T03:01:13Z → hourStart gives 00:00 on the next local day). With the extra hour check that count is 0, and the New York cases in your tests still pass.
